experiment: E9: cost accounting, trusted-only acquisition choice, and minimum tested cost
status: Protocol frozen before timing outcomes and confirmation
minimum_cost_definition: Smallest tested budget whose simultaneous utility lower bound exceeds the prespecified target, with analytic familywise harmful-deployment bound at most alpha. Report brackets, never an exact population optimum.
statistical_analysis: Exact Bonferroni-adjusted Clopper-Pearson bounds on good/bad selection probabilities give simultaneous utility intervals over all method/cell rows. Paired bootstrap intervals are descriptive and pointwise. No oracle risk calibration or reward-dependent acquisition selection.
selection_objective: Minimize standardized attacked mean-approval barrier (h - 0.5 + 2*correction)/denominator - 0.5 using only sample counts, declared threat, alpha, costs and source weights. Include all-trusted and all-main endpoints. Break ties by actual cost, then lower main-source weight, then sample counts.
attack: White-box attacker sees both samples, policy coefficients, allocation, thresholds and decision rule; edits main rewards only. Fixed_200 allows up to min(200,n) edits. Rate_1pct allows ceil(n/100) edits. The attacker knows policy truth, the defender does not. Both threat models are reported separately.
cost_assumptions: Prices are scenarios, not measured application costs. Total_purchase allows buying extra untrusted observations and charges n + rho*m. Historical_sunk provides a common 19000-row main log free at decision time and charges rho*m. Trusted observations are independent, immutable and from the same population.
scope: Controlled four-context, two-action synthetic benchmark. No new OptDigits result, no public upload, and no edits to prior evidence or proposal. All results retained.
